procedural_history.originating_court: Additional Sessions Court(Adhoc-1), Palakkad in Sessions Case No.221 of 2009. Order dated 13.09.2010
procedural_history.impugned_order: Final judgment and order dated 13.06.2016 passed by the High Court of Kerala at Ernakulam in Crl. A. No. 1837 of 2010.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court of Kerala at Ernakulam in Crl. A. No. 1837 of 2010 allowed the appeal in part by maintaining the conviction but reducing the sentence imposed on the appellant.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellant (Accused No.2) felt aggrieved by the High Court's order and filed a special leave petition, which was granted, resulting in Criminal Appeal No. 1409 of 2018 in the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal.

issue.issue_text: Whether any case is made out on facts and in law for interfering in the quantum of sentence awarded to the appellant by the High Court.

facts: The incident in question was old, having occurred in 2007.
The appellant had already served 1 year and 3 months of the 3-year jail sentence imposed by the High Court.
The appellant had no prior criminal history, with this being their only case.
Out of the three original accused, one had been acquitted (given the benefit of doubt).
law: The Court has the discretion to interfere with the quantum of a sentence if the facts and circumstances of the case warrant such an intervention.
application: The Supreme Court considered the cumulative effect of the specific facts of the case.
It weighed the significant passage of time since the offense, the portion of the sentence already served, the appellant's clean record, and the acquittal of a co-accused.
Based on these combined factors, the Court was of the "considered opinion" that the appellant had successfully made a case for interference with the sentence.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court decided to interfere with the sentence. It reduced the appellant's jail term to the time "already undergone" but, as a modification, increased the fine from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 1.5 lakh. Failure to pay the enhanced fine would result in an additional year of imprisonment.

arguments.issue_text: Whether any case is made out on facts and in law for interfering in the quantum of sentence awarded to the appellant by the High Court.
appellant_arguments: The appellant, feeling aggrieved by the High Court's order, filed an appeal arguing that the quantum of the sentence should be interfered with and reduced.
respondent_arguments: The text does not specify the respondent's arguments, but as the opposing party (the State), their position would have been to defend the High Court's sentence and argue against any interference or reduction.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: A court has the discretion to impose a fine of more than one lakh rupees depending upon the facts of each case.
obiter: The appellant's case falls under clause (a) and is governed by Section 55 (1) of the Abkari Act.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: Keeping in view the facts that the incident in question is of the year 2007; the appellant has undergone jail sentence of 1 year 3 months out of three years total period of jail sentence awarded by the High Court; the appellant was never involved in any criminal activity except the case at hand; and out of three accused, one was given the benefit of doubt, the Court is of the considered opinion that the appellant has made out a case for interference in the quantum of sentence awarded to him by the High Court.
legal_tests_applied: It is mandatory for the Court to impose a fine while awarding jail sentence and secondly, it cannot be less than Rs. one lakh. However, the Court has discretion to impose fine more than Rs. one lakh depending upon the facts of each case.
why_appellant_lost: The appellant did not succeed in having the fine reduced or waived because the court has the discretion to impose a fine of more than Rs. one lakh, and in this case, it exercised that discretion to enhance the fine from Rs. one lakh to Rs. one lakh fifty thousand.
why_respondent_won: The respondent succeeded in having a substantial fine imposed and enhanced because the governing law makes it mandatory for the court to impose a fine of at least Rs. one lakh and grants the court discretion to impose a higher amount based on the facts of the case.
policy_considerations: The significant passage of time since the offense occurred in 2007.
The fact that the appellant had already served a substantial portion (1 year and 3 months) of the three-year sentence.
The appellant's clean prior record, as he was never involved in any criminal activity apart from the present case.
A sense of parity in justice, noting that one of the three co-accused had been acquitted (given the benefit of the doubt).
